scorer_3_result.same_house_style_A_reason: Shares C's warm-core/cool-periphery chiaroscuro formula and soft painterly brush treatment, but object modeling (tombstones, tent, crates) is flatter and less sculptural/detailed than C's carved pillars and effigy, so it reads one tier below the anchor's density.
scorer_3_result.same_house_style_D_reason: Uses the same warm-fire/dark-forest palette idea as C but the shading is noticeably flatter and more uniform (crates, bedrolls, rocks), with an overlaid-looking light-shaft effect that doesn't integrate the way C's torch glow and ambient occlusion do; reads as a cruder pipeline than the anchor.
key_defects_A: Tombstone-like standing-stone props and tent read as plain, under-modeled shapes with little carved/sculptural detail (a NEW defect vs the incumbent, likely a pass2-populate hallucination — a campsite has no reason for gravestone-shaped monoliths)
Crate linework leans slightly graphic/decal-like rather than fully painted form
Grass/ground texture comparatively plain next to C's stonework detail
key_defects_D: Crates, bedrolls, rocks use flatter, more uniform local-color shading with minimal form modeling
Sunbeam light-shaft effect looks overlaid/airbrushed, doesn't integrate with the painterly forest
Trees/rocks are simplified silhouettes lacking directional light modeling seen in A/C

auditing_agent_direct_visual_read.note: Supplementary, not a formal panel score — the dispatching agent viewed all 4 images directly via the Read tool.
auditing_agent_direct_visual_read.observation: C (crypt_dense) is unambiguously denser/more painterly than both A and D: carved relief, distinct warm/cool separation, visible oil-brush texture. A and D are close to each other in overall craft level (same flat/cel-shaded feel on crates/logs/bedrolls) — the regen does NOT clearly close the house-style gap. A introduces 2-3 tall gray rectangular monolith props on the left tree-line that read as out-of-place gravestone shapes for a living campsite scene — a new repetition/hallucination-adjacent defect not present in D.

verdict: KEEP INCUMBENT — do not replace camp_clearing_night_v1 with this regen. Rationale: (1) the panel is statistically underpowered (n=1 scorer with full data + 1 supplementary non-blind visual read, not the required 5), so no gate pass can be certified; (2) even the available signal is not a clean win — scorer 3's numbers modestly favor the candidate (7 vs 5 craft, 6 vs 4 house-style) but the candidate has its own new defect (out-of-place monolith props) and neither plate closes the gap to crypt_dense_v1 the owner is calibrating against; (3) re-running the IDENTICAL proven recipe (same LoRA/strength/order-law/greybox) did not materially change the outcome, which itself is evidence the regression is NOT a broken-parameter bug — it's a base-dependent pass-value gap (PANEL7, 2026-07-02: 'the passes rescue sparse bases; strong textured bases mostly need only the staging pass') plus never-validated outdoor lighting templates and non-architectural focal-feature vocabulary. Closing the gap needs a PROMPT-LANGUAGE fix (denser/more specific sculptural clutter nouns for outdoor scenes) as a follow-up, not a same-recipe reroll.
